strategy.observation: Transistor offers private podcasts, and its customer base includes enterprise companies and small businesses, which makes it plausible that many of the shows on the platform are business podcasts rather than hobby projects.
strategy.offer_link: If Transistor works with B2B and enterprise podcast programs, an audio-editing and show-notes partner could help those customers publish consistently and reduce production overhead for teams using private or externally facing shows.
hypotheses: Transistor may field requests from customers who need help producing and maintaining business podcasts, especially private/internal shows.
The Partnerships Lead may be open to referral or service-partner conversations that add value for Transistor customers without requiring in-house production services.
Some Transistor customers may prefer to outsource editing and show-note creation rather than handle it internally.
strategy.angle: Since Transistor supports private podcasts for enterprise and small-business customers, you may have B2B shows on the platform that need editing and show notes support.
strategy.fit_reason: There is a plausible fit because Transistor serves business podcast customers and offers private podcasts, but the facts do not show that Transistor needs or sells production services, so the link to audio editing and show notes is indirect.

draft.subject: Private podcast support
draft.body:
Hi — I help B2B brands with podcast audio editing and show notes, so teams can publish without adding more in-house work.

Since Transistor supports private podcasts and works with small businesses and enterprise companies, my guess is some of your customers are running business podcasts that need a bit of production support.

Do you ever point those teams to outside editing or show-notes help, or is that not part of the partnership side?
